slos.description: explain, with examples, that civilisations throughout history have systematically studied living things e.g., the history of numbers from sumerians and its development to the present arabic system;
describe terminating and non-terminating (recurring and non-recurring) decimal as rational and irrational numbers;
identify the set of real numbers as a union of sets of rational and irrational numbers;
identify the properties of real numbers (closure, commutative, associative, identities, inverse, distributive properties);
identify radicals and radicands;
convert radical form to exponential form and vice versa;

apply the laws of exponents to simplify expressions with real base and exponents:
x^m · x^n = x^(m+n),
(xy)^m = x^m y^m,
(x^m)^n = x^(mn),
(x/y)^m = x^m / y^m, where y ≠ 0,
y^0 = 1,
x^m / x^n = x^(m-n), where x ≠ 0.
convert a number in ordinary form (common form) to scientific notation and vice versa;

convert logarithmic form into exponential form and vice versa:
(i.e., a^x = y ↔ log_a(y) = x, a > 0, y > 0 and a ≠ 1);
solve problems related to SLO 2.2.1;

describe the following laws of logarithms:
a. log_a(mn) = log_a(m) + log_a(n),
b. log_a(m/n) = log_a(m) - log_a(n),
c. log_a(m^n) = n log_a(m),
d. log_m(n) = log_a(n) / log_a(m),
where a > 0, a ≠ 1;
solve problems using the given laws of logarithm (without using log and antilog tables) in SLO 2.3.1.
describe mathematics as the study of pattern, structure, and relationship;
identify the sets denoted by N, Z, W, O, P, Q and by other symbols;

solve problems using the following operations on sets:
a. union,
b. intersection,
c. difference,
d. symmetric difference,
e. complement;

describe the following fundamental properties of union and intersection of two or three sets:
a. commutative property of union,
b. commutative property of intersection,
c. associative property of union,
d. associative property of intersection,
e. distributive property of union over intersection,
f. distributive property of intersection over union,
g. De Morgan's laws;

draw Venn diagrams to represent:
a. union and intersection of sets,
b. difference of sets,
c. complement of a set,
d. symmetric difference of sets;
apply concepts of set theory up to three overlapping sets to solve world problems;
describe ordered pairs and Cartesian product;
solve problems based on ordered pairs and Cartesian product;
describe a binary relation;
find the domain and range of a binary relation.
define function;

describe:
a. into function,
b. into and one-one function (injective function),
c. onto function (surjective function),
d. one-one and onto function (bijective function);

identify:
a. into function,
b. into and one-one function (injective function),
c. onto function (surjective function),
d. one-one and onto function (bijective function);
describe the concept and notation of a function, its domain, codomain and range;
determine the value of a function for given values of dependent and independent variables;
apply concepts from functions to real world problems;
interpret the functions mentioned in SLO 4.1.2;
describe the inverse of a function and its notation;
find the inverse of a function and its domain and range;
describe the composition of functions and its notation;
plot graphs of a constant function, identity function, linear function and absolute valued functions;
determine the domain and range of a function through the graph;
apply concepts of absolute valued functions to real-world problems.

apply the following algebraic identities to solve problems:
a. (a + b)^2 + (a - b)^2 = 2(a^2 + b^2),
b. (a + b)^2 - (a - b)^2 = 4ab,
c. (a + b)(a - b) = a^2 - b^2,
d. (a + b + c)^2 = a^2 + b^2 + c^2 + 2ab + 2bc + 2ca,
e. (a + b)^3 = a^3 + 3ab(a + b) + b^3,
f. (a - b)^3 = a^3 - 3ab(a - b) - b^3,
g. a^3 + b^3 = (a + b)(a^2 - ab + b^2),
h. a^3 - b^3 = (a - b)(a^2 + ab + b^2);

factorise the expression of the following types:
a. ka + kb + kc,
b. ac + ad + bc + bd,
c. a^2 ± 2ab + b^2,
d. a^2 - b^2,
e. a^2 ± 2ab + b^2 - c^2,
f. a^4 ± a^2b^2 + b^4 or a^4 + b^4,
g. ax^2 + bx + c,
h. (a^3 ± 3a^2b + 3ab^2 ± b^3),
i. a^3 ± b^3;
define zeros of a polynomial;

solve the expression to find the remainder using remainder theorem;
(Note: when a polynomial of degree up to 4 is divided by polynomial of degree up to 2)
apply concepts of remainder and factor theorem to solve problems.

subtopics.name: 6.1 Highest Common Factor and Least Common Multiple

slos.description: determine the highest common factor (H.C.F.) and the least common multiple (L.C.M.) of algebraic expressions using factorisation;
apply H.C.F., L.C.M. and their relationship in solving problems;
describe rational expressions;
simplify algebraic fractional expressions or rational expressions involving basic operations of +, -, ×, ÷;
distinguish between proper and improper rational fractions;

represent an algebraic fraction into partial fractions when its denominator consists of:
a. non-repeated quadratic factors,
b. repeated quadratic factors.
define linear equation in one variable;
solve linear equation with real coefficients;
solve problems based on linear equations;
solve radical equations reducible to linear form;
verify the solution (discarding extraneous roots);
define absolute valued functions in one variable;
solve equations involving absolute valued functions in one variable;

define inequalities:
a. less than (<),
b. greater than (>),
c. less than or equal (≤),
d. greater than or equal (≥);
solve linear inequalities with real coefficients in one variable and represent the solution on the number line;
solve absolute valued inequalities in one variable and represent the solution on the number line;
plot linear inequality with two variables on graph;
solve two linear inequalities with two variables graphically;
interpret the regions in the plane that are bounded by two linear inequalities involving two variables.
describe rectangular coordinate system in plane;
describe magnitude of a vector, equal vectors, negative of a vector, unit vector, zero/ null vector, position vector, parallel vectors;
determine magnitude of a vector;
represent translation by a vector;
represent vectors as directed line segment;
explain addition and subtraction of vectors;
explain multiplication of a vector by a scalar;
apply the concepts given in SLOs 8.2.1 and 8.2.2 of two vectors geometrically;
represent a vector in a Cartesian plane by describing the fundamental unit vectors i and j;
apply concepts from geometrical problems involving the use of vectors (such as parallel and perpendicular lines in geometrical shapes).
describe coordinate geometry;
explain distance formula by locating the position of two points in coordinate plane;
determine the distance between two given points;
calculate the midpoint of a line segment;
solve word problems related to midpoint formula;
explain inclination and gradient of a line;

subtopics.name: 9.4 Standard Form of Equation of a Straight Line

slos.description: convert the general form of the equation of a straight line into the form mentioned in SLO # 9.4.1;
determine the x and y intercepts from the given linear equation;
apply the concepts of coordinate geometry to real world problems.
define locus;
describe simple loci of points in two dimensions;

explain the locus of points under the given conditions:
a. at a given distance from a given point,
b. at a given distance from a given straight line,
c. equidistant from two given points,
d. equidistant from two given intersecting straight lines;
solve problems using the method of intersecting loci for sets of points in two dimensions which are mentioned in SLO 10.1.3.
differentiate between a mathematical statement and its proof;
differentiate between an axiom, conjecture and theorem;
formulate simple deductive proofs [algebraic proofs that require showing the LHS to be equal to the RHS].

describe the conditions for following polygons and solids to be similar:
a. triangle,
b. square and rectangle,
c. cube and cuboid,
d. semi-circle and circle;
solve problems by applying the relationship between area and volume of similar figures as mentioned in SLO 12.1.1;
analyse whether the two figures are similar as mentioned in SLO 12.1.1.

apply the following properties to solve related problems:
a. if two opposite sides of a quadrilateral are congruent and parallel, it is a parallelogram,
b. in a parallelogram:
   i. the opposite sides are congruent,
   ii. the opposite angles are congruent,
   iii. the diagonals bisect each other;
c. the line segment, joining the midpoints of two sides of a triangle, is parallel to the third side and is equal to one half of its length;

solve real world problems that involve the properties mentioned in SLO 13.1.1 of the following polygons:
a. triangle,
b. rectangle,
c. square.
describe the sexagesimal system (degree, minute and second);
convert an angle from D°M'S" to decimal form or vice versa;
define radian;
convert an angle from degree to radian and vice versa;
identify quadrants and quadrantal angles (0, ±90°, ±180°, ±270°, ±360°);
identify the signs of trigonometric ratios in different quadrants;
calculate the values of trigonometric ratios and their reciprocals for 30°, 45° and 60°;

subtopics.name: 14.3 Application of Pythagoras' Theorem and Trigonometric Ratios

slos.description: determine the unknown sides or angles in a right-angled triangle by applying Pythagoras' theorem and the sine, cosine and tangent ratios for acute angles (30°, 45°, and 60°);
explain the fundamental trigonometric identities i.e., sin^2(θ) + cos^2(θ) = 1, 1 + tan^2(θ) = sec^2(θ), 1 + cot^2(θ) = cosec^2(θ);
prove different trigonometric relations using the trigonometric identities mentioned in SLO 14.4.1;
describe the angle of elevation and depression;
solve word problems involving angle of elevation and depression in a right-angled triangle.
